rv.q: It’s a sincere gift nonetheless, a loving call for human compassion and a singing homage to its titular architect.
The attention here is on the emotional connection established between actors and audience through Ms. Goldberg’s bright-hued portraits of people reflecting on the odd byways of their lives.
The stage and TV versions were each a sensation.
The Whoopi Monologues have been reborn for a new generation and are not showing their age.
The Whoopi Monologues is a glorious incarnation of Whoopi Goldberg’s pop culture-centric magnum opus.
More than four decades after its original incarnation premiered, this fresh take on Ms. Goldberg’s breakthrough work decidedly stands up.
This sterling revival demonstrates that, with the right actors and creative talent, The Whoopi Monologues is strong enough to make an impact without its namesake star.

Yes, you’ll marvel at the acting abilities of the five extraordinary women now portraying Goldberg’s signature alter egos, but the awe will derive from how well much of the material holds up, for better and worse.
Young (Purlie Victorious, Purpose) is flawless, whether discussing the Anne Frank house in Amsterdam, eyes full of wonder, or describing the airplane meal.
And there can be no competition for the enjoyment of seeing these five fine actresses taking on the roles in person and making them their own.
The evening ends with all five actresses on stage, celebrating their diversity and dancing to disco-era songs, a fitting finale to a fun show.
The five-member cast of “The Whoopi Monologues” is talented in their own right, some famously so.
The Whoopi Monologues is a worthwhile evening that deserves credit for creatively rethinking a long-established piece.
The main reason to see The Whoopi Monologues is to catch five actresses demonstrating their easy mastery of the stage.
It's quite a show, but not quite as impressive as watching one talented actor perform all five roles.
But while The Whoopi Monologues serves as a showcase for its five performers much as it did for its creator, the divvying up reduces rather than enhances its impact.
As a showcase for a quintet of gifted comedic actresses, The Whoopi Monologues still delivers.
If you’re a fan of Nettles, you will not be disappointed in the showy role she wrote for herself.
The work not only holds up, it soars.

cn.t: Critics generally praise this reimagining of Goldberg's 1984 solo show with five actresses, celebrating strong performances while questioning whether dividing the material sacrifices the original's virtuoso impact.
